messages:
maria: Heads-up — we had 5 noisy GPU-util pages overnight from eu-west-1-training. They were all the nightly retrain jobs, not user-facing. Thinking we should tweak paging vs ticketing so oncall only gets pages for real customer impact. Thoughts?
aj: Can you paste the alert rule that fired?
maria: Sure — here's the rule that alerted:
```yaml
alert: GPUHighUtilization
expr: avg_over_time(node_gpu_util[5m]) > 0.9
for: 1m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-high-util
```
sam: That `for: 1m` is pretty aggressive for batch jobs. Retrains will spike for short periods. We should differentiate by job tag or node pool label (training vs infer).
leo: Agreed. We also need grouping to avoid 5 separate pages when a whole cluster warms up. Group by `cluster` and `gpu_type` in alertmanager, or use `vector( count_over_time(...) )` style.
maria: Proposal: two-tier rule — page if avg>0.9 for 5m AND (node_role="inference" OR queue_backlog>0), otherwise create a ticket when avg>0.75 for 10m. Also add repeat suppression if same cluster fired <30m ago.
aj: Sounds reasonable. Example combined rule idea:
```yaml
- alert: GPU_Paging_Candidate
  expr: avg_over_time(node_gpu_util{role="inference"}[5m]) > 0.9
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
- alert: GPU_Ticket_Candidate
  expr: avg_over_time(node_gpu_util[10m]) > 0.75
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
```
sam: For suppression: Alertmanager route that drops pages if `cluster_meta: maintenance=true` or if last_fired(cluster) < 30m. We can use `repeat_interval` and `group_interval` to coalesce.
leo: Also add a mute window for scheduled nightly retrains: 02:00-06:00 UTC for clusters tagged `scheduled-training`. Pages should convert to tickets during that window.
maria: Good call. We still want emergency paging for OOMs or node flapping. So keep separate high-severity rule: `node_gpu_oom_total > 0` => page immediately.
aj: Let's not forget cost signals — if we are paging because of transient cloud spot eviction spin-ups, we should suppress until X spot churn rate threshold. Otherwise ops gets paged for noisy cloud events.
sam: Operational playbook additions:
- When a page is suppressed, Alertmanager should create a low-priority ticket with stacktraces/log links
- Include top-5 pods on GPU and `kubectl top` snippet in annotation
- Provide quick rollback button in console if rollout caused spikes
maria: I'll draft the Alertmanager routes and updated Prom rules. Goal: reduce page-to-ticket ratio to <5% for scheduled workloads.
leo: Can we add a Grafana panel for "pages avoided by suppression" so we can measure false-suppresses?
maria: Yes — metric `alertmanager_suppressed_alerts_total{reason!="auto-snooze"}` + dashboard.
ops-bot: deploybot: New route PR opened by @maria: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/alerts/pull/142 — awaiting review.
aj: Reviewing now. Quick checklist: ensure `for` durations, group_by labels, and mute windows are documented in runbook. Also set a hard escalation: if suppressed alert repeats 3 times within 2h, force a page.
maria: Added that to the PR. Also noted runbook updates. Will schedule a short sync with oncall to review. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks — this should cut 80% of the noise I saw last week.
leo: If we see regressions we can flip feature flag `suppressive-paging-v2` back off. Keep an eye on SLOs.
maria: Sync invite sent for tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Agenda: review PR, validate Grafana panels, and test suppression playback on staging.
ops-bot: oncall: pagers muted for scheduled-training between 02:00-06:00 UTC (config applied).
